works.title: Moravec 1998 (on hardware overhang and AI timelines)
works.why: Source of the forecast that compute would become cheap enough for human-level AI around the 2020s, which the piece says is holding up.

works.title: Meta-Learning with Memory-Augmented Neural Networks (and related work)
works.why: Cited among foundational work on implicit/emergent meta-learning in neural networks.

works.title: Wang et al. 2018 (meta-reinforcement learning)
works.why: Cited as evidence that meta-learning emerges spontaneously from training on many related tasks.

works.title: Botvinick et al. 2019a
works.why: Further citation supporting the claim that meta-learning emerges inevitably from training on interrelated tasks.

works.title: Clune 2019 (AI-generating algorithms)
works.why: Cited among background work on emergent meta-learning in neural networks.

works.title: Schmidhuber 2015/2018
works.why: Cited as background on meta-learning and universal learning algorithms.

works.title: Weng 2018/2019 (meta-learning survey posts)
works.why: Cited as further reading on implicit meta-learning.

works.title: Jukebox
works.why: Cited as another scaling demonstration (raw audio music generation) that preceded GPT-3's release.

works.title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
works.why: Quoted epigraph framing the discomfort people feel toward brute, unglamorous approaches like scaling.

works.title: T5
works.why: Cited as a prior large model and as an example trained only once like GPT-3.

works.title: LeCun 2019 (on whether deep learning is part of AGI)
works.why: Quoted skepticism ('is the cake a lie') that the piece responds to in arguing GPT-3 is real progress toward AGI.

works.title: Language Models are Few-Shot Learners (GPT-3 paper)
works.why: Reports the GPT-3 scaling results and benchmark numbers the whole essay is built around.

works.title: Hernandez & Brown 2020 (compute-efficiency scaling study)
works.why: Used to estimate how training costs for a fixed performance level fall over time.

works.title: Thompson et al. 2020
works.why: Criticized as an example of a poorly-controlled scaling study that failed to find clean scaling curves.

works.title: Turing-NLG
works.why: Used as the prior largest dense language model benchmark that GPT-3 far surpassed.

works.title: CTRL
works.why: Cited as one of the prior large language models whose performance suggested scaling might soon plateau.

works.title: Meena
works.why: Cited as a prior large model, and its perplexity-vs-human-ness ratings are used as another scaling data point.

works.title: MegatronLM
works.why: Cited as one of the prior large models used to argue scaling curves might bend before GPT-3 disproved this.

works.title: GPipe
works.why: Cited as one of the prior large models used as a reference point for scaling trends before GPT-3.

works.title: AlphaGo Zero
works.why: Used as a comparison point for GPT-3's compute cost and as an example of scaling up simple architectures.

works.title: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
works.why: Shows the power-law scaling curves for loss vs compute/data/parameters that the article extends with GPT-3.

works.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding
works.why: Cited as evidence of how GPT-3's question-answering performance scales with model size.

works.title: Schrimpf et al. 2020 (language models and brain activity)
works.why: Cited as evidence that larger language models' internal activity becomes more human brain-like.

works.title: Warstadt et al. 2020 (linguistic biases and data scale)
works.why: Cited as evidence that human-like linguistic biases increase with more training data.

works.title: Very Deep VAEs (Child 2020)
works.why: Cited as an example of VAEs matching GAN-quality image generation once made very deep.

works.title: Vahdat & Kautz 2020 (NVAE)
works.why: Cited alongside Child 2020 as evidence deep VAEs catch up to GANs at scale.

works.title: Hill et al. 2019
works.why: Cited as supporting evidence for emergent generalization from scale in agents.

works.title: Chaplot et al. 2017
works.why: Cited among supporting work for emergent generalization in trained agents.

works.title: Yu et al. 2018
works.why: Cited among supporting work for emergent generalization in trained agents.

works.title: Lake 2019
works.why: Cited among supporting references for generalization from training on richer tasks.

works.title: Interactive Agents Group 2020
works.why: Cited among supporting references for emergent generalization in trained agents.

works.title: Dojolonga et al. 2020
works.why: Cited as evidence that image classifiers transfer and develop human-like errors at scale, including after apparent plateau.

works.title: Big Transfer (BiT)
works.why: Cited as an example classifier that transfers and robustifies with human-like errors at scale.

works.title: ResNeXt
works.why: Cited as another example of a classifier CNN that benefits from scale.

works.title: Noisy Student
works.why: Cited as an example of a classifier that transfers and robustifies at scale.

works.title: ViLBERT / VideoBERT
works.why: Cited as examples of multimodal learning producing better representations from less data.

works.title: BigGAN
works.why: Cited as an example of a model that stabilizes and benefits from unusually large minibatches at scale.

works.title: StyleGAN
works.why: Cited as showing disentanglement emerging with sufficiently deep embeddings.

works.title: GQN (Generative Query Network)
works.why: Cited as an example where enough samples force factorized, disentangled representations.

works.title: AlphaStar
works.why: Cited as reaching human level via hundreds of competing self-play agents, exemplifying blessings of scale.

works.title: MetaMimic
works.why: Cited as imitation-learning DRL that generalizes across hundreds of tasks when trained on a deep net.

works.title: Dactyl
works.why: Cited as an example of implicit meta-learning emerging from training on millions of domain randomizations.

works.title: DD-PPO
works.why: Cited as outperforming classical robot planners after scaling compute by two orders of magnitude.

works.title: Procgen
works.why: Cited as showing agents generalize to unseen levels only once trained on thousands of levels.

works.title: CoinRun
works.why: Cited alongside Procgen as showing generalization emerging only at large numbers of training levels.

works.title: AlphaZero
works.why: Cited as achieving superhuman Go by training a bigger model on richer self-play data without search illusions.

works.title: MuZero
works.why: Cited as showing an RNN trained end-to-end to predict reward can implicitly learn tree search, surpassing AlphaZero.

works.title: GPT-f
works.why: Cited as a related model showing scaling-driven generalization, in the formal-math domain.

works.title: iGPT (Image GPT)
works.why: Cited alongside Vision Transformer as evidence that scaling unsupervised models works outside text too.

works.title: Vision Transformer
works.why: Cited as evidence that simple scaled-up architectures match complex specialized alternatives in a new domain (images).

works.title: Orseau et al. 2020
works.why: Cited for the idea that big models encode countless interpolating sub-models over the data.

works.title: Viering & Loog 2021
works.why: Cited regarding phase transitions in learning as models grow large enough for abstract solutions to emerge.

works.title: Cambria & White 2014 (NLP research eras)
works.why: Source of the figure depicting hypothetical S-curves of progress in natural language modeling used to frame the pretraining thesis.

works.title: Collobert et al. 2011 (natural language processing almost from scratch)
works.why: Quoted on whether leveraging the small entropy gap between humans and n-gram models can teach grammar and world knowledge.

works.title: Shannon 1951 (prediction and entropy of printed English)
works.why: Source of the original human-subject estimate of English entropy used to frame how close models get to human-level prediction.

works.title: Teahan & Cleary 1996
works.why: Cited for the lowest n-gram-model entropy estimate used as the baseline models must beat to show real understanding.

works.title: The Legacy of Hiroshima ("The Quiet Enemy")
works.why: Source of the Teller/Bohr anecdote used as an analogy for scaling being feasible once believed possible.

works.title: One Billion Word Benchmark dataset paper
works.why: Source of the 1BW benchmark used (then dropped) to compare GPT-2/GPT-3 perplexity to human performance.

works.title: The Human Use of Human Beings
works.why: Quoted on how publicizing that a hard problem is solvable accelerates independent discovery, applied to scaling.

works.title: GShard
works.why: Cited as an example of Google Brain's practical, deployment-oriented scaling work rather than pure scaling bets.

works.title: Hestness et al. 2017 (deep learning scaling paper)
works.why: Cited as an early scaling-law paper, used to note Chinese AI companies' (Baidu) research contributions.

works.title: ZeRO-2 (Microsoft)
works.why: Cited as evidence another organization besides OpenAI has reached trillion-parameter-scale training.

works.title: SayCan
works.why: Cited as an example of a language model actually taking real-world actions via a robot, supporting the agency argument.

works.title: An Introduction to Wittgenstein's Tractatus
works.why: Source of the heliocentrism anecdote used to argue a counterintuitive framing can still be the correct one.
